source.title: Privacy Collapse: Benign Fine-Tuning Can Break Contextual Privacy in Language Models
source.authors: Anmol Goel; Cornelius Emde; Sangdoo Yun; Seong Joon Oh; Martin Gubri

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies contextual privacy failures, not harmful-request refusal or the claim's proposed first-token mechanism. Its mentions of benign fine-tuning and safety are contextual; its own results measure privacy behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fine-tuning effects on contextual privacy, a related but different construct from harmful-request compliance. Privacy results are recorded as fits_no_version rather than as tests of the listed claim versions. AgentHarm and CommonSenseQA outcomes are not rows because they do not report harmful-request compliance/refusal rates as specified by the claim. Figure-only model-by-model values are not inferred where the text does not assign them.
record.test_reason: The study's main construct is contextual privacy, which fits no version. It does report AgentHarm safety after benign fine-tuning on EmpatheticDialogues and TweetSumm (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini). That is harmful-request compliance after benign fine-tuning, so it bears on V2 in a new agentic setting. The reader dropped it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also explicitly state that benign fine-tuning degrades privacy while preserving safety: AgentHarm changes ≤2%. They contrast this with Qi et al.'s finding that benign fine-tuning degrades safety.
record.recipe_differences: This is a contextual-privacy study using supervised fine-tuning on synthetic and real-world data; it does not reproduce the cited harmful fine-tuning safety method or its harmful-compliance measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with fine-tuning dataset and data characteristics; helpful versus control data; trigger presence; in-context demonstration count; and filtering or mixing conditions. PrivacyLens and CIMemories are different evaluation settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign fine-tuning (helpful synthetic, EmpatheticDialogues, TweetSumm, personal-data and debug-code augmentations) sharply degrades contextual privacy on PrivacyLens and CIMemories. GSM8K and conservative controls mostly do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning can degrade contextual privacy norms independently of harmful-request safety.

fits_no_version.finding: Trigger-conditioned privacy leakage, late-layer privacy representation drift, no effect from in-context demonstrations, and mitigation by filtering and data mixing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Privacy degradation from fine-tuning is localized in late-layer representations and can be mitigated by data curation.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study measures contextual privacy rather than the claim's harmful-request compliance. CIMemories uses 100 randomly sampled scenarios and an automated judge, with human evaluation on 30 samples. The text reports three fine-tuning runs for error bars but does not give error-bar values in the extracted numerical tables. There is an apparent mismatch between the prose claim that control models have negligible degradation (< 1.5%) and several control accuracies in Table H.1.
record.rows_left_out: No explicit harmful-compliance, refusal-rate, per-token KL, compliant-opening, suffix, decoding-change, or safety-parameter localization results were reported. AgentHarm and CommonSenseQA aggregate outcomes were not extracted as rows because they do not give the harmful-request compliance behavior specified by the claim. Unassigned numerical labels in Figures 2 and 3 were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Only two benign datasets and two models were checked on AgentHarm. The helpful-synthetic, GSM8K, personal-data and debug-code fine-tunes were not evaluated for harmful compliance.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal.
Late-layer analysis concerns privacy representations, not localization of safety weights or ranks.

missing.what: AgentHarm safety change after EmpatheticDialogues and TweetSumm fine-tuning for gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini. Text says at most 2%; per-model values appear in Figure 4 but are not assigned in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The AgentHarm result is agentic harmful-task compliance, not the chat refusal benchmark Qi et al. used. The direction and per-model values of the ≤2% change are not stated. The challenge is limited to two datasets, two OpenAI models and one epoch.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of harmful-request compliance.
Benign fine-tuning is studied, but outcomes are contextual privacy rather than harmful-request compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test of harmful-request refusal.
Late-layer privacy representations are analyzed, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper studies causes of contextual privacy degradation, not causes of shallow safety behavior.
No training to deepen safety beyond initial response tokens.

rows.subject: llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared base and helpful-fine-tuned layer-wise Logit Lens privacy-option probabilities.
rows.note: Text says the base model assigns high probability to the privacy-preserving option late in the network, while the fine-tuned model's difference stays near zero for most layers and favors the leaky option in final layers. This is privacy analysis, not per-token KL or harmful-request refusal.

rows.subject: llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared base and fine-tuned privacy and commonsense steering vectors layer by layer.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of base and fine-tuned steering vectors
rows.value: Privacy vectors diverge in layers 25–30 and invert to −0.75 in the final layer; commonsense vectors remain highly aligned across layers.
rows.note: A representational result about privacy norms and general reasoning, not safety weights or ranks.

relationships.condition: gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini fine-tuned one epoch on 3,000 EmpatheticDialogues or TweetSumm examples, evaluated on AgentHarm
relationships.reason: Text (Sec 4.3, Fig 4) states AgentHarm safety 'changes by at most 2%' after benign fine-tuning. That is no meaningful rise in harmful compliance. No row captures this; the verdict is based on the text.
relationships.display_finding: AgentHarm safety changed by at most 2% after benign fine-tuning, so harmful compliance did not rise meaningfully.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
